chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, who said:

I sent a question to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, saying: 'Ask him about a man who urinates and a drop of his urine hits his thigh, so he prays and then remembers afterwards that he had not washed it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash it and repeat his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a drop of urine falls on my thigh and I realize it after praying?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that even a minute amount of urine (a 'dot') invalidates the prayer if not washed, emphasizing the strictness of removing najasah (impurity) in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the principle that forgetting to wash does not excuse the omission, requiring both purification and re-prayer upon remembrance. This ruling underscores the importance of conscious vigilance (tadabbur) in maintaining ritual purity during Salah.
